A partnership's assessable income includes its share of amounts that are included in the net amounts on which other entities are assessed under the provisions of the Act listed in s 12-5(2). These amounts include the partner's share of the partnership's income (s 12-5(3) ITAA97).  A partnership's deductions include its share of expenses and outgoings incurred in gaining or producing the partnership's exempt or non-assessable non-exempt income as well as any expenses incurred in relation to its exempt income or non-assessable non-exempt income (s 12-5(4) ITAA97).   Partnerships are not subject to the tax imposed by the Medicare Levy Surcharge Act 1986 (MLSA) or the Medicare Levy Act 1986 (MLA). However, the partnership may need to consider whether any of its individual members are subject to the MLSA or MLA.  A partnership will generally have no capital gains or losses. However, where a partner disposes of a partnership interest, the CGT consequences depend on whether the partner is a ‘trading stock’ dealer (s 70-10 ITAA97).  A partnership is not entitled to deductions for gifts, donations or contributions made to charities (s 25-5 ITAA97). In addition, a partnership does not pay income tax on the distribution it makes to its partners (ITAA36 s 44).   A partnership is not entitled to deductions for dividends received on shares in another company (s 25-5 ITAA97).
